    tsdst.utils.dsn_getTable¶

    tsdst.utils.dsn_getTable(sql, user, dialect, dsn, pw=None, create_engine_args=None, read_sql_args=None)[source]¶

    Load data into python from a SQL database.

    Requires a DSN or connection string. Uses SQLAlchemy to make the connection, and closes the connection on completion. See https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/engines.html for help building connection strings.

    Parameters:
    sqlstr, or list

    A string containing the SQL query to run (It should be something that returns a table), or a list of sql statements to return multiple tables (tables are returned as a list of pandas dataframes, in this case).

    userstr

    The username for the database application, if applicable.

    dialectstr

    The database flavor (oracle, mysql, etc.)

    dsnstr

    Can either be a saved DSN from your computer, or a string that represents all the relevant information provided in a DSN. It can also be a host:port combination. See sqlalchemy documentation for more details.

    pwstr, optional

    The password for the database application that matches the user specified, if applicable. If None or ‘’, getpass will ask for a password. If there is no password, just leave it blank. The default is None.

    create_engine_argsdict, optional

    A dictionary containing arguments to be passed to SQLAlchemy’s create_engine function.

    read_sql_argsdict, optional

    A dictionary containing arguments to be passed to pandas’ read_sql function.

    Returns:
    datapandas dataframe or list

    A dataframe (or list of dataframes) containing the returned data.

    Notes

    The DSN may contain a host, port, database path, and query parameters. Those components are parsed before credentials are assigned, so characters such as @, /, and : in passwords are escaped correctly. The engine is disposed even when a query or write raises an exception. These helpers build credentialed DSN URLs; SQLite uses a different URL form and can be used directly through a SQLAlchemy engine and pandas’ SQL functions.
